The prompt is UNCHANGED on purpose: the only difference from the six batches that measured 0/5 is the SEED below. Changing the wording as well would make the arm uninterpretable.

seed.why:
🔴 THE CONTROL THAT REFUTES MY OWN ROW. The row says the model 'picks the sibling' — glossary_adopt_standards wins over the advertised, answerable glossary_propose_batch on 5 of 5 runs. THE COMPETING EXPLANATION IS THAT IT IS NOT A CONTEST AT ALL: the fixture book has `seed: []`, so it has NO ONTOLOGY, and there is nothing to add kinds and attributes TO. Adopting a standard set first is then not a rival choice, it is the precondition, and the model is right.

THIS IS NOT A NEW HYPOTHESIS — IT IS A FINDING THIS REPO ALREADY MADE AND I DID NOT APPLY TO THIS ROW. scenarios-c-gbuild-control.json records, for composition_build_cast_and_graph, the IDENTICAL chain (glossary_list_system_standards -> glossary_adopt_standards -> glossary_task_provide_input, 5/5, batch c-r1-recheck) and says in as many words: 'I filed that as a SIBLING-WINS failure; it is a PRECONDITION — a glossary cannot be built onto a book with no kinds, and adopting first is the correct move.' The same seed took kg_triage_schema_write from blocked to proven.

WHAT THIS ARM DECIDES. If glossary_propose_batch is now CALLED, the row's diagnosis is refuted: surfacing was never the issue and no sibling won anything — the turn was spending itself on a missing precondition, and the row must be WITHDRAWN with that recorded. If it is STILL 0/K with an ontology present, the precondition explanation is dead, the sibling-wins diagnosis survives its strongest challenge, and the row is on much firmer ground than it has ever been.

EITHER OUTCOME MOVES THE ROW. That is why this is worth a run rather than another argument.
